newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - April 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - April 22.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY
- Welfare Minister Geraldine Fraser-Moleketi remained defiant on Monday in the face of renewed calls for the suspension of controversial government plans for a new child support benefit scheme.

- Foreign investors chasing high yields have piled into the gilts market this year, taking the net purchases so far to almost eight billion rand from less than three billion rand for the whole of last year.

- BMW SA will attract an additional one billion rand foreign investment spin-off into South Africa's motor component industry from the group's plan to manufacture the new 3-series for the world market.

- Mining group JCI Ltd has become the latest South African company to despatch a high-ranking delegation to Zaire in an attempt to salvage millions of rands worth of business interests and potential project contracts.
- Provinces have reached agreement with government at the budget council that there will be no more "bail-outs" from central fiscus on overspending.
BUSINESS REPORT

- The losers in the bids for casino licences in Nelspruit and Witbank on Monday slammed the objection process against the preferred finalist, Tsogo Sun, as little more than a public relations exercise.

- Billions of rands of investments in tourism, agricultural and infrastructural development along the Lubombo corridor in northeastern KwaZulu Natal were announced on Monday at a Lubombo spatial development initiative workshop in Richards Bay.
- Soekor, the state owned oil exploration company, said on Monday South Africa's first "black" oil would be produced within a fortnight from the Oribi oilfield, some 140 km southwest of Mossel Bay.
- Richards Bay has been shortlisted as a possible site for a new Volkswagen aluminium engine assembly plant, sources close to the company said on Monday.

- Cape Town businessman Neill Bernstein, who is picking up an 84 percent stake in IB Joffe Ltd, the JSE-listed manufacturer and distributor of camping and outdoor gear, has co-written a musical on Nelson Mandela and Oliver Tambo which is to be launched nationally and internationally later this year.
SAKE BEELD

- President Nelson Mandela pours cold water on the Congress of South African Trade Unions (Cosatu) saying his government will not necessarily favour trade unions aligned to his African National Congress because it serves all sections of the population, not just workers.
- Gengold Ltd announced a profit of 87.7 million rand for the three months to end-March compared to 68.9 million rand in the preceding quarter.
THE STAR

- The parents of a 14-year-old boy facing a charge of culpable homicide after a 9-year-old girl was run over and killed at the weekend were on their way back from Taiwan on Monday to arrange a lawyer for their son.
- A gang of 16 heavily armed men stopped a security truck at a roadblock they had erected on the N1 north of Pietersburg and made off with about four million rand on Monday.

- Information given to the Truth and Reconciliation Commission in secret by former Vlakplass informer Joe Mamasela will be handed to ex-Vlakplaas commander Dirk Coetzee's defence team following an order by the Durban High Court on Monday.

- Greater Johannesburg's public finances are on the brink of chaos after the decision by the National Party and the Democratic Party to withdraw their support from the ruling ANC which needs their votes to pass the 1997/98 budget in June.
